headline_drivers: Q4 2025 / FY earnings beat with 7.9% YoY revenue growth and EPS turning solidly positive; stock jumped ~10% on the print as investors focused on AI/data‑center memory strength (earnings reported 2026-02-27, discussed in Schwab/YouTube segment)

Mix shift toward higher‑margin Integrated Memory for AI/data‑center workloads, with margins improving even as Advanced Computing and Optimized LED margins are squeezed; investors treating this as an AI infrastructure lever rather than a legacy hardware vendor (earnings commentary Feb–Mar 2026)

Forward earnings upgrades: Street models now bake in ~13–14% EPS growth next year and ~60%+ longer‑term earnings CAGR, driving a major P/E re‑rating despite consensus target still around $27–29 (MarketBeat / Simply Wall St updates through mid‑May 2026)

Breakout to new all‑time highs and inclusion on momentum / top‑20d / gapper screens (+150%+ over 2 months, 52‑week range $16–$54) is pulling in systematic and retail momentum flows despite low incremental volume vs. 10‑day average
summary: The move in PENG is primarily a post‑earnings re‑rating and AI‑infrastructure story: the February 27 earnings report showed a clear turn with 7.9% revenue growth, solid profitability (TTM EPS ~$0.75 on $1.35B revenue), and expanding margins in the Integrated Memory segment tied to data‑center/AI demand, which investors now view as the company’s core growth engine. As that AI‑memory narrative has spread via media coverage and analyst model updates (EPS growth forecasts raised into the teens near‑term and >60% longer term), the stock has broken out to all‑time highs and been picked up by momentum screens, amplifying the move far beyond the fundamental step‑change and pushing the multiple to a rich ~70x+ earnings even though the Street’s average target (~$27–29) still sits well below the current price. In other words, the market is reacting to a perceived AI‑driven margin and growth inflection plus technical momentum, not to a single new customer win or M&A announcement.
